memory_candidates.content: A verification-bar grep that matches literal path text (e.g. 'state.json' or 'archive/state.json' adjacent to a redirect) will silently miss hand-rolled writes that route through shell variables instead (e.g. "$ARCHIVE_STATE_FILE" > "${ARCHIVE_STATE_FILE}.tmp"). Baselining the grep against ONE known pre-conversion file is not sufficient to trust it everywhere -- baseline it against every distinct file/pattern shape in scope, since a variable-based site can produce zero matches both before and after conversion, proving nothing either way. When this gap is found, verify that script's correctness directly (bash -n, --dry-run smoke test, or a full fixtured run) rather than relying on the grep.

check-extension-docs.sh's 'deployed script content drift' finding (deployed .claude/scripts/X differs from agent-system/extensions/*/scripts/X) is the EXPECTED, transient state of any source-store-only edit before the next redeploy cycle -- it is NOT a defect for a general-implementation-agent to fix by invoking deploy-headless.sh, whose own header restricts automated invocation to skill-orchestrate's inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint only. Distinguish this from a genuinely actionable check-extension-docs.sh failure like a stale index-entries.json line_count (Rule R), which IS a source-store fix within an implementer's scope, via generate-context-line-counts.sh --write.

Scripts guarded by deploy-root-guard.sh (e.g. generate-context-line-counts.sh) refuse to run when invoked directly from the agent-system/extensions/*/scripts/ source-store location, even when their actual read/write target is a source-store file (like index-entries.json) rather than anything under .claude/**. This is because they resolve PROJECT_ROOT via SCRIPT_DIR/../.., which only lands correctly two levels under a deployed .claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/ tree. Invoke such scripts via their DEPLOYED path (bash .claude/scripts/<name>.sh) even when the fix itself belongs in the source store.
